knownLimitations: Qualification cases and delivery evidence are synthetic. An attestor signature proves control of the agreed wallet, not carrier identity, physical delivery, or document authenticity. There is no carrier identity oracle, insurance escrow, or settlement. Studionet RPC can be intermittently unavailable or rate-limited; an initial production read failure and successful retry are recorded in evidence/production-registry-retries.json. Cases are append-only and not pruned.
name: ParcelCourt
short: Review delivery claims against a frozen handoff promise, attested evidence, two-party challenges and independent semantic consensus.
problem: Delivery disputes depend on natural-language handoff promises and evidence that may be incomplete, manipulated or contradictory.
solution: ParcelCourt supports a delivery-claim lifecycle from consent and frozen promise through evidence submission, a distinct attestor, semantic adjudication, two-party challenges, second-round deliberation and finalization. The production app reads paged canonical case records and hash-linked history from Studionet, and provides wallet-validated signing and post-transaction receipt/state reconciliation.
outcomes: Leader and validators independently classify handoff_matches_promise, authorized_recipient_supported and evidence_sufficient. The strict vector and bounded deterministic verdict are validated; the second round incorporates both parties' challenge text; disagreement cannot become approval or alter parameters, actors, deadlines or rules.
